conclusion: The original remaining-case matrix defines R4 as zh-CN/noisy file quality and R5 as a stable-path own-App-PID resource attachment. It does not make source-to-AAR identity or a recursive static-component inventory an R4 or R5 acceptance assertion.

The current W3 roadmap explicitly lists exact recursive runtime binary composition/source mapping, production integration/notification, and independent release review among the remaining W3 work. Therefore these items are not optional later evidence that may be discarded when judging W3 overall closure.

The current documents require the evidence outcome (exact source/binary mapping and recursive final composition) but do not prescribe one unique cryptographic proof construction. A proposed proof method must be reviewed for sufficiency; it must not be silently weakened to partial archive, build-log, or four-ORT-member correspondence.

R4 quality failures/limits and R5/W8 resource-budget gaps remain independently open. Provenance/release evidence cannot substitute for their quality or resource acceptance, and quality/resource observations cannot substitute for the provenance/release gates.

finding.title: W3 closeout requirements lack a single named acceptance-matrix row and sufficient-proof definition
finding.impact: Treating the older R1-R5 matrix as exhaustive would incorrectly remove current W3 production/release requirements; treating partial provenance receipts as the requested exact proof would incorrectly close them. Either interpretation could produce a false W3-complete claim.
finding.rootCause: The current roadmap adds production/release closeout work outside the original R1-R5 case table, while the individual evidence receipts deliberately describe their own insufficiency.
finding.requiredResolution: Retain both items in the W3 closeout ledger under a distinct production/release category, separate from R4 quality and R5/W8 resource acceptance. Before closure, define the accepted proof artifact, its source/build/AAR boundaries, recursive component coverage, and independent review criterion.

rootCauseFallbackCheck.assessment: No fallback may reclassify the absence of an original R4/R5 row as authorization to drop current W3 closeout work. Archive completeness, build-log correspondence, and selected ORT-member equality are documented partial evidence with visible limitations, not alternate success paths.

recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES_TO_W3_CLOSEOUT_CLAIM_ONLY: do not mark W3 complete until the distinct production/release gates and the independently open R4/R5 requirements are each resolved or explicitly scope-disposed by the authorized owner.
